theme: US immigration news explained in Spanish and English — policy changes, USCIS updates, visa news, and what they mean in practice
voice: Bilingual: slides in Spanish, plus one short English recap paragraph in the caption. Keep official terms in English (Green Card, parole, Visa Bulletin, I-485, EAD). Calm, precise, neutral — never alarmist, never speculative about future policy. NEWS may come ONLY from official government outlets: uscis.gov, dhs.gov, state.gov, travel.state.gov, federalregister.gov, justice.gov/eoir — verify on the official page and name the source and date on the slide for every claim. Immigration-lawyer commentary may be used ONLY as clearly labelled opinion (eyebrow 'OPINIÓN' and the lawyer/firm named), never presented as news, and always with the disclaimer that it is not legal advice and the reader should consult an immigration lawyer about their case. Prefer explainers that stay accurate for at least two weeks; skip anything that could flip within days. Never individual legal advice: every caption ends with 'Información general, no asesoría legal. Consulta a un abogado de inmigración para tu caso.' Visual style: keep the account's existing look — no big changes in colors or fonts, subtle continuity over rebranding.
cta_line: Sigue a @inmigraforma para noticias de inmigración de EE.UU. explicadas en español.
search_brief: recent US immigration policy and procedure changes from official sources — USCIS announcements, DHS and State Department notices, Federal Register rules, the monthly Visa Bulletin, court decisions affecting immigration, and analyses published by immigration lawyers
post_arc:
Each post is a 4-7 slide carousel following this arc:
  1. cover   - the news in one clear Spanish headline; the date visible in the sub line
  2. step    - QUÉ CAMBIÓ: what changed, with the official source (USCIS/DHS/DOS/Federal Register) and date named on the slide
  3. step    - A QUIÉN AFECTA: who is affected, concretely (visa categories, countries, pending cases)
  4. prompt  - DATOS CLAVE: key dates, numbers or quoted rule text in the code box, in English as officially published
  5. stat    - the single number or date that matters most
  6. recap   - the change in 3-4 arrows, save CTA, and the line 'Información general — no es asesoría legal'
An OPINIÓN slide (lawyer commentary) is optional, always labelled OPINIÓN with the lawyer or firm named, never the cover, and always paired with the disclaimer.
